subject: Discovery Recap & Procurement Next Steps — Acme Enterprise
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery Recap & Procurement Next Steps — Acme Enterprise

Alex — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have a shared record and clear next steps. Happy to update if I missed anything.

Key pain points you called out:
- Latency spikes on peak traffic for in-product assistants (esp. recommendation flows) causing conversion drop-offs
- High per-token costs on current vendor for high-volume batch reranking
- Need for stronger controls/auditability for PII-sensitive queries to meet internal compliance

Current stack & constraints:
- Models: Mix of hosted LLMs (vendor X) for generation + in-house smaller models for reranking
- Infra: GCP us-west primary, off-peak batch jobs run in us-central
- Procurement: standard enterprise procurement with a 3-person procurement committee (Ravi listed below), security review required (SOC2 + data handling questionnaire)

Success criteria you shared:
- Reduce 95th percentile generation latency by ~30% for interactive flows
- 40% reduction in per-unit inference costs for batch reranks
- Pass Red team / security checklist for PII handling and key management

Immediate next steps:
1) I attached a lightweight requirements_matrix.xlsx that captures the success metrics + sample traffic profile you shared. Please confirm or edit.
2) Can you confirm the procurement stakeholders and core decision timeline? My understanding from today: Ravi Patel (Procurement), Sarah Li (CTO), decision window target: by end of Nov.
3) We can put together an initial commercial guardrail (ballpark pricing + commit options) for your procurement team — would a target budget range help at this stage?
4) Propose a short procurement readout with procurement + security on Oct 20 to discuss SOW, MSA, and data handling details.

If that aligns, I’ll follow up with an initial commercial estimate and a proposed agenda for the Oct 20 readout.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: requirements_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ravi Patel <ravi.p@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap & Procurement Next Steps — Acme Enterprise

Thanks Marissa — this is great and captures the discussion. A few clarifications from our side:

- Procurement/stakeholders: Confirming Ravi Patel (Procurement) and Sarah Li (CTO) are the core decision-makers. I’ll also pull in our Security Ops lead (Tanya Brooks) for the SOC2/data handling portion.
- Timeline: We’re aiming to select a vendor by the end of November with contracting finished in early December. Key gating item is the security questionnaire + a short pilot to validate latency/cost claims.
- Budget guardrails: At a high level, we’re targeting $200k–$400k ARR for initial committed capacity depending on pilot results. Open to committed vs consumption mix.

Request: Can you include a simple 12-month cost estimate for three scenarios — baseline (consumption), committed 6-month, committed 12-month — that maps to expected QPS and monthly token volume? That will help Ravi.

I’ll coordinate Ravi on availability for the Oct 20 meeting; tentatively sounds good.

—Alex
Product Lead, Platform
Acme Enterprise
alex.j@acme.com

Subject: Re: Discovery Recap & Procurement Next Steps — Acme Enterprise

Appreciate the clarity, Alex — that timeline and budget range are helpful.

Per your ask, attaching a short capacity & estimate PDF (redwood-capacity-estimate.pdf) with a ballpark for three scenarios:
- Baseline (consumption): estimate shown with no commit — higher per-unit, flexible
- Committed 6-month: discounted per-token rate with a modest throughput SLA
- Committed 12-month: best unit economics + dedicated slot allocation option (suitable if you want predictable latency at peak)

High-level commercial guardrail (very rough at this stage):
- 200k ARR: likely covers a small committed tier with modest throughput (best-effort latency targets)
- 300–400k ARR: moves you into dedicated pool + stronger 95p latency targets and longer-term discounts

Next steps I’ll take this week:
1) Draft a 1-page commercial guardrail (ballpark pricing + what we need from procurement to proceed).
2) Propose Oct 20 procurement readout agenda and share a calendar invite with proposed attendee list (Procurement, Security Ops, CTO, Redwood Solutions Eng).
3) Share the pilot statement of work template and a short checklist for the security questionnaire so Tanya/Ravi can triage.

If that works, I’ll send the invite and attachments by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: redwood-capacity-estimate.pdf (3 pages)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Discovery Recap & Procurement Next Steps — Acme Enterprise

Quick internal alignment — looping you both for visibility.

Notes for prep:
- Marissa: I’ll draft the 1-page commercial guardrail. Suggest we present three options: Consumption, 6-month commit, 12-month commit (include ballpark $/token and an example monthly invoice).
- Vivek: can you draft a short note on latency SLAs we can promise for the 12-month dedicated option and any constraints (model size, seq length)? We should avoid overpromising on 95p for generated content until we validate on pilot data.
- I’ll also prepare a recommended pilot SOW (2–4 weeks, sample dataset, pass/fail criteria aligned to the success metrics Marissa captured).

Will sync before the Oct 20 readout; aiming to have commercial guardail and SOW draft by EOD Oct 14.

—Neha
